The review includes 1,794 primary studies from 2017-2026 and 95 secondary studies, with every decision released in Dataset S1. Each primary study was assigned to a 13-category taxonomy and graded as simulation, prototype or testbed, production data, production deployment, or not determinable from the abstract. Of 1,003 studies with a determinable level, 66.2% used prototypes or testbeds, 18.0% simulations and 15.8% production data or deployments. A 93-study synthesis core, appraised from indexed abstracts, shows production deployments of cascading-failure prevention, trace- and graph-based root-cause analysis and predictive autoscaling, and production-trace evaluations of cold-start mitigation. Edge reliability and physical AI rely mainly on simulations and testbeds. AI-agent reliability uses tool-grounded diagnosis, explicit safety properties, trace-driven repair and workload-aware scheduling, while empirical studies show that agent frameworks remain fragile. Conclusions are limited to the documented corpus. The principal gaps are production evidence for edge-native systems, shared resilience benchmarks and dependable agentic operations.

entries.title: Optimal Sampling and Transmission Policy for Information Freshness in Gossip Networks
entries.abstract: We study the optimal sampling and transmission policies for a transmitter communicating with n gossiping receivers with the objective of tracking a source's status over time using a semantic freshness metric: Version Age of Information (VAoI). The transmitter observes the version changes in the source, and can acquire a new information version by paying a sampling cost. The receivers gossip, allowing information exchange among each other without direct transmission. Gossiping can save on transmission cost, but it may propagate stale version information, necessitating transmitter intervention. With imperfect communication links, we formulate an infinite horizon average cost Markov Decision Process (MDP) in order to jointly optimize receivers' VAoIs, sampling and transmission costs in a time slotted fully connected (FC) gossip network. We first solve the MDP using Relative Value Iteration (RVI) algorithm. Then, we prove that the sampling decision has a threshold structure in the transmitter VAoI. Further, under reliable gossiping links, we show that transmission and idling has an VAoI-difference threshold structure with minimum VAoI activation. Numerical results obtained using RVI show that the optimal policy consistently outperforms natural baselines. These results characterize how source sampling, direct transmission, and receiver gossip should be jointly coordinated for cost-aware semantic freshness in gossip networks.
entries.comment: Potential IEEE journal publication

entries.title: Distributed Intelligent Ad Hoc Routing Agents for Communication at Protests During Internet Shutdowns
entries.abstract: Governments around the world are increasingly using internet shutdowns to block digital communication. Internet shutdowns are particularly dangerous during political protests, as they inhibit protesters' ability to organize and communicate critical, potentially life-saving information and may be used to prevent awareness of state-based violence. Recent prior works have explored secure, private messaging systems for use during political protests and internet shutdowns but have encountered long delivery delays or low delivery rates under challenging conditions. In this work, we explore the use of distributed, adaptive, social- and congestion-aware heuristics and efficient communication patterns to create an intelligent ad hoc routing protocol in which network agents learn and leverage the network social environment and monitor and respond to dynamic network congestion behaviour to route messages in a time- and resource-efficient manner. Through this exploration, we contribute an intelligent algorithm and protocol which overall achieves comparable or higher delivery rates relative to the leading dynamic clique routing protocol which it extends while also transmitting messages through notably fewer carriers and, when network devices have larger amounts of buffer storage, transmitting fewer message-related packets. We additionally contribute a further understanding of routing limitations and challenges and conceptualizations of extensions of intelligent dynamic clique routing to overcome them.

entries.title: SLA-Aware Task Offloading in the IoT Edge-Cloud Continuum: Class-Weighted Deep Reinforcement Learning Against an Exact Optimum
entries.abstract: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) is often used to decide where Internet of Things (IoT) tasks with different latency limits run in the edge-cloud continuum, yet some methods give every missed task the same penalty and few compare their agents with an optimal policy. This benchmark study builds four offloading systems small enough to solve exactly by dynamic programming and measures reward and learner against the optimum. A bonus for a met limit makes each miss cost its penalty plus the bonus, which shifts the class weights of published per-class rewards. A class-blind penalty stays 65% to 118% above the optimal cost even with a perfect learner, while a corrected per-class penalty comes within 0.13% of the optimum. With a per-class reward, tuned proximal policy optimization (PPO) agents come within 9% to 11% of the optimum in the smallest system, and the corrected one beats a tuned reservation rule in 9 of 10 seeds. In larger systems the agents stay 41% to 76% above the optimum, and a tuned rule beats their mean. Training ten times longer does not close this gap, and a PPO-Lagrangian agent with reachable targets does no better than the per-class reward.

entries.title: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
entries.abstract: Accurate indoor localization on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to the tension between modeling fidelity and computational efficiency. Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) enables low-cost deployment using existing Wi-Fi infrastructure but is heavily distorted by multipath propagation. Transformer-based solutions mitigate these effects but their quadratic complexity limits real-time edge deployment. Ultra-Wideband (UWB) provides geometrically precise ranging yet requires dedicated infrastructure. We present MambaLoc, a cross-modal distillation framework that improves the accuracy-efficiency balance in CSI-based localization. MambaLoc uses a linear-time Selective State Space Model (Mamba) as a lightweight CSI student, guided during training by a UWB-Transformer teacher. A Feature Alignment Module bridges the representational gap between heterogeneous RF modalities, allowing the CSI model to inherit UWB-derived geometric structure without UWB hardware at inference. A probabilistic Gaussian Mixture regression head models multi-modal spatial ambiguity from multipath effects, avoiding the physically implausible averaging of deterministic regression. Evaluations on a real-world dataset show MambaLoc achieves a median localization error of 0.230 m, reducing error by 22.2% over a standalone Mamba baseline, while requiring 65.1% fewer FLOPs and 58% lower inference latency than Transformer-based approaches.
entries.journalRef: M. Bahnassy, O. Saqr, H. Rizk, and M. Youssef, "MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation," Proceedings of the 27th IEEE International Conference on Mobile Data Management (MDM), 2026, pp. 177-183

entries.title: From Radio Measurements to Sensing Services: A 3GPP Perspective on Multi-UAV Tracking with Networked ISAC
entries.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) can turn radio measurements into networked sensing services, but accurate position estimates alone do not ensure useful tracking. Missed targets, late acquisition, track interruptions and aging observations also shape the information available to an application. This article examines tracking of noncooperative unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from a Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) perspective. It connects sensing-service requirements and network architecture to three information interfaces: receiver search regions, measurement context and track validity. A five-UAV case study in a 3GPP urban scenario and a ray-traced San Francisco scene illustrates the tradeoff between target coverage and extra outputs, the distinction between acquisition and ongoing continuity, and the value of testing a static mission envelope before adding adaptation. An observation-age example explains how a state predicted to the present can still rely on old evidence. The resulting lessons are to align receiver search with requested coverage, preserve measurement time and uncertainty, and assess coverage, ambiguity and timeliness together. We conclude by pointing out fruitful avenues for further work in sensing design, calibration and service validation.
